# Chapter 3: The Sub-Basement

The stairs down to the sub-basement ran colder than the reading room ever managed. Priya Raman went first and carried the torch.

Emmett Rourke had lied about the night shifts. Delia Foss understood that plainly now, and understood also that Emmett Rourke had been paid to lie about them.

"I'm sorry," Emmett Rourke said. "Halloran told me the arrangement was routine."

So Halloran was a real person after all. Priya Raman set the torch down on the shelf and turned to face Emmett Rourke squarely.

The eleven months stood stacked against the far wall in four grey boxes. Nobody had destroyed a single page of them. Somebody had simply moved the boxes to where nobody would ever think to look.

Delia Foss put her hand flat on the topmost box and found it warm, as though it had been moved that same hour.
